teaching_goal: An anticodon is three tRNA bases that pair with a matching mRNA codon.

review_notes.hook_claim: L22-p1: the anticodon is three bases complementary to a codon; the tRNA with anticodon UAC pairs with AUG.
review_notes.analogy: Puzzle pieces that only fit their match.

scenes.title: How does a tRNA find its spot?
scenes.narration: How does a tRNA know where to go? It reads three letters at a time. Three mRNA bases make a codon. The tRNA has three matching bases, called the anticodon. Here's the start codon, A-U-G. The tRNA with U-A-C pairs with it. A matches U. U matches A. G matches C. Like puzzle pieces that only fit their match. An anticodon is three tRNA bases that pair with a matching mRNA codon. Swipe.
